The two things with a hard deadline are the Acme contract (Thursday) and the Vega CAD approval, which is blocking Meera.

**Hold the price at 8% off. Don't take 12%.**

The numbers don't support conceding:

- 12% off drops gross margin to 25%, below our volume ceiling of 8% off (28% margin). Going to 12% needs founder approval.
- Tarang's own claim doesn't hold up. Leela Krishnan says a competitor quoted 10% below list (Rs 10.8 lakh), yet they're asking for 12% off (Rs 10.56 lakh). They want more than their alleged competing offer.
- No stock pressure forcing a discount. We have 52 K2 units in the warehouse against 34 committed for Oct to Nov, with 60 units a month of capacity.

What argues for staying engaged rather than digging in:

- Tarang paid on time on their 2025 order (6 printers at 5% off).
- They have 3 more plants that may order in 2027, which makes this order a foot in the door, not a one-off.

So the move is to hold at 8% and use the future volume as the reason, not a concession. Offer 8% off now and a better tier if they convert those 3 plants in 2027. That keeps margin at 28%, answers the competitor angle on value, and gives Leela a path to a better price without us breaking our own ceiling.

I can draft the counter for Leela if you want.

- **Not started:** launch webinar, sales training, price list update, spare parts SKUs.
- **Budget:** Rs 18.2 lakh of Rs 24 lakh spent (76%).
- **Risks:** the 19 Oct CE lab slot is the only one before release. A failed test pushes release to mid-November. Neha Joshi holds two tasks due within 4 days of each other.

Want me to update any of these tasks or draw a Gantt chart of the remaining work?

Counter at 8 percent. Don't give 12.

The numbers: 12 percent off drops you to Rs 10.56 lakh at 25 percent margin; 8 percent off is Rs 11.04 lakh at 28 percent. Leela's competitor quote is 10 percent below list, so she's asking you to beat it by 2 percent for no reason.

- Your ceiling without founder sign-off is 8 percent, and it still beats the repeat-buyer case: Tarang paid on time last year.
- Capacity is not the excuse it might look like. You hold 52 K2 units and make 60 a month against 34 committed for Oct-Nov [entity:7c1e] [entity:91aa], so you can absorb 40 units easily and want the volume.
- The real asset is 2027: three more plants could order. That's the lever to protect margin now.

Options:

- Hold list: Rs 12 lakh, 34 percent margin. You likely lose to the 10-percent competitor.
- Counter at 8 percent (recommended): Rs 11.04 lakh, 28 percent, no approval needed. Offer a written 2027 three-plant commitment as the reason.
- Match at 10 percent: Rs 10.8 lakh, about 26.5 percent, needs your approval. Only if Leela won't move off the competitor and you want to lock the relationship.
- Give 12: Rs 10.56 lakh, 25 percent, needs your approval. Leaves 2 percent on the table versus the competitor quote.

If you want, I'll draft the counter to Leela at 8 percent with the 2027 hook.
